Delisting or Failure to Satisfy a Continued Listing Rule or Standard; Transfer of Listing</span></div><div><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:10pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">On July 17, 2026, Shore Bancshares, Inc. (the &#8220;Company&#8221;) provided initial notice to The Nasdaq Stock Market, Inc. (&#8220;Nasdaq&#8221;) that Shore United Bank, N.A., which is the Company&#8217;s wholly owned subsidiary bank (the &#8220;Bank&#8221;), had made payments to a law firm of which Mr. Louis P. Jenkins, Jr., a director and former member of the Audit Committee, is a partner. The payments made to the law firm were for legal services in connection with various loan matters. The payments, which totaled $10,555, were for legal services rendered by the law firm from February to April 2026, during which period Mr. Jenkins was serving on the Company&#8217;s Audit Committee. As a result of such payments, the Company believes it did not comply with Nasdaq&#8217;s audit committee composition requirements under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5605(c)(2) (the &#8220;Rule&#8221;). Among other things, the Rule requires that each member of the Audit Committee meet the criteria for independence set forth in Rule 10A-3(b)(1) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;). In order to resolve this violation, effective as of July 16, 2026, Mr. Jenkins resigned from the Company&#8217;s Audit Committee. The Audit Committee is now comprised of four members who all meet the requirements of the Rule.</span></div><div id="i2c0e959c1ced4fe08a1a69bd29e6b257_10"></div><div
